before:
name: external_browser_surface_macos_smoke
description: |
  macOS/MoltenVK integration smoke for ExternalBrowserSurface. It creates a real IOSurface-backed
  source render target, turns that IOSurface into a Mach send right, resolves the right through the
  same receiver path used by an Electron producer, GPU-copies it into the stable resident image,
  waits for the post-fence PRESENTED release, and reads the resident image back to assert its pixel.
  This is intentionally a source RTT rather than a fake CPU image: every macOS import, Vulkan copy,
  layout, fence, and retain/release step is live. Requires a macOS Vulkan window.
operations:
  - create:
      box: external_browser_surface_renderer
      name: external browser surface renderer
      frame: { x: 40.0, y: 40.0, w: 320.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options
          
          prop<Window>(window)
          prop<Renderer>(renderer)
          
          Options.enableHDR = false
          Options.profiling = false
          
          once.renderer {
              window = Window("External browser surface macOS smoke")
              Renderer(window)
          }
          
          println("external browser surface renderer ready")
          start(renderer::run)
  - create:
      box: external_browser_surface_smoke
      name: IOSurface Mach-port import and copy
      frame: { x: 320.0, y: 140.0, w: 350.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.Target
          import afield.media.browser.*
          import java.io.ByteArrayInputStream
          import java.util.Base64
          import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList
          import javax.imageio.ImageIO
          import org.lwjgl.vulkan.VK10.*

          val releases = CopyOnWriteArrayList<BrowserFrameRelease>()
          val source = RenderToTexture(renderer) {
              width = 64
              height = 64
              format = VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM
              useDepth = false
              colorSampled = true
              exportMetalIOSurface = true
              clearColor = vec(0.125, 0.5, 0.875, 1.0)
              debugName = "external-browser-macos-smoke-source"
          }
          val surface = MacExternalBrowserSurface(
              renderer,
              ExternalBrowserSurfaceSpec(64, 64, BrowserSurfacePixelFormat.BGRA8_UNORM, slotCount = 2),
          ) {
                  releases.add(it)
              }

          val ioSurfaceRef = source.colorImageRefs.first()!!.exportMetalIOSurfaceRef()
          val ioSurfaceId = MetalIOSurface.ioSurfaceId(ioSurfaceRef)
          require(ioSurfaceId != 0L) { "MoltenVK did not export an IOSurface" }
          val ioSurfacePort = MetalIOSurface.createMachPort(ioSurfaceRef)
          require(ioSurfacePort != 0) { "could not create an IOSurface Mach port" }
          require(
              surface.offerFrame(
                  ExternalBrowserFrame(
                      streamId = 1,
                      frameId = 1,
                      slot = 0,
                      width = 64,
                      height = 64,
                      pixelFormat = BrowserSurfacePixelFormat.BGRA8_UNORM,
                      handle = ExternalBrowserImageHandle.MacIOSurfaceMachPort(ioSurfacePort),
                  ),
              ) == BrowserFrameOfferResult.ACCEPTED,
          )

          renderer.renderList.others["external-browser-macos-smoke-source"] = source
          renderer.renderList.others["external-browser-macos-smoke-copy"] = Target { command, _ ->
              surface.prepareSampledImagesFor(command)
          }

          var ticks = 0
          loop {
              ticks++
              val release = releases.firstOrNull()
              if (release == null && ticks < 600) {
                  frame()
              } else {
                  require(release != null) { "no browser release after $ticks ticks" }
                  require(release.reason == BrowserFrameReleaseReason.PRESENTED) {
                      "browser frame release failed: $release"
                  }
                  val html: String = TexturePreviewCache.capture(
                      renderer,
                      surface.imageView.image,
                      VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM,
                      64,
                      64,
                      VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL,
                      64,
                  ) ?: throw IllegalStateException("resident texture readback failed")
                  val encoded =
                      Regex("base64,([^']+)").find(html)?.groupValues?.get(1)
                          ?: throw IllegalStateException("PNG payload missing")
                  val image = ImageIO.read(ByteArrayInputStream(Base64.getDecoder().decode(encoded)))
                  val argb = image.getRGB(32, 32)
                  val red = (argb ushr 16) and 255
                  val green = (argb ushr 8) and 255
                  val blue = argb and 255
                  println("external-browser-macos id=$ioSurfaceId rgb=$red,$green,$blue release=$release")
                  require(red in 28..36 && green in 124..132 && blue in 219..227) {
                      "unexpected copied pixel $red,$green,$blue"
                  }
                  println("external-browser-macos PASS")
                  end()
              }
          }
              .end {
                  renderer.renderList.others.remove("external-browser-macos-smoke-copy")
                  renderer.renderList.others.remove("external-browser-macos-smoke-source")
                  surface.close()
              }
  - connect: { parent: external_browser_surface_renderer, child: external_browser_surface_smoke }
  - launch: { box: external_browser_surface_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: { wait: pending }
  - launch: { box: external_browser_surface_smoke, property: code }

name: splat_sequence_streaming
description: |
  Play a sequence of PlayCanvas .compressed.ply splat files as 4D video: fifteen files a frame,
  arranged in a ring around the viewer, decoded straight into one GPU buffer, with a scrubbable
  play head. One graphics child box under the stable `agent_graphics_context` parent.

  There is deliberately no committed sample sequence — one is tens of megabytes and would be
  somebody's artwork rather than a fixture. Point `sequenceDir` at your own directory of
  `.compressed.ply` frames; the box says how to make one if the directory is missing, and stops
  rather than throwing.

  What it demonstrates, and why each piece is not the obvious thing:
    - CompressedSplatPly.readRaw + GaussianSplatRenderer.packInto: the quantized payload goes
      straight to the 16-float GPU layout, written absolutely into the mapped storage buffer, so
      there is no intermediate float table and no copy. 22 ms for 310k splats where the
      decompress-then-pack route took 59 ms.
    - Fifteen sources into ONE cloud: one buffer, one draw, and one sort order correct ACROSS
      sources rather than fifteen locally-correct orders that interleave wrongly.
    - The ring is fifteen ROTATIONS, not translations: each capture already sits ~1-1.6 in front of
      its own origin, being a depth map from a camera at the origin, so rotating about Y puts each
      panel at its natural distance. Translating as well clumps them.
    - SortMode.None plus a CPU back-to-front sort in packInto: no depth-key compute pass, no radix
      sort, no per-frame pre-target. The sort of 310k longs is 2.8 ms parallel.
    - SplatTransport.advance() returns false on the display frames where the resolved frame did not
      move — six in seven at 12 fps into 90 Hz — which is why scrubbing is cheap.
operations:
  - create:
      box: splat_sequence_streaming
      name: Splat Sequence Streaming
      frame:
        x: 60.0
        y: 60.0
        w: 420.0
        h: 110.0
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.GaussianSplatRenderer
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.GaussianSplatRenderer.Blend
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.GaussianSplatRenderer.SortMode
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.GaussianSplatRenderer.SplatSource
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.SplatSequence
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.SplatTransport
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.Target
          import java.io.File

          /*
          ---- knobs: edit and re-run this box ------------------------------------
          No committed sample: point this at your own frames. To make some, take a .ply per
          frame and run PlayCanvas splat-transform over each:
              splat-transform frame_0001.ply frame_0001.compressed.ply
          */
          val sequenceDir = File(System.getProperty("user.home"), "Downloads/splat-sequence")
          val slots = 15 // sources shown at once, one per direction around you
          val fps = 12.0 // source frame rate, independent of the display rate
          val sortEachFrame = true // false + an order-independent blend == no sort at all
          val blend = Blend.Over // Over / Additive / Screen / Multiply / Max
          val splatSize = 2.5f // these splats are ~2 mm across, so they need help
          val alphaBoost = 1.6f
          val arcDegrees = 200.0 // spread the slots over this much of the circle
          val cameraBack = 2.6f
          val cameraUp = 1.1f
          /*
          2.2 is sRGB-to-linear and is CORRECT: SwapChain prefers B8G8R8A8_SRGB, so the target
          encodes back on write. Lowering it double-encodes -- brighter than the data, which is a
          legitimate artistic move but not a fix for a dark scene.
          */
          val colorGamma = 2.2f

          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

          if (!sequenceDir.isDirectory) {
              println("no sequence at $sequenceDir")
              println("Point `sequenceDir` above at a directory of .compressed.ply frames.")
              println("PlayCanvas splat-transform writes them: splat-transform in.ply out.compressed.ply")
              println("Any 3DGS .ply will do as a source; a single frame repeated also works.")
          } else {

              val sequence = SplatSequence.fromDirectory(sequenceDir, cacheFrames = 160)
              val capacity = sequence.peakWindowSplats(slots)
              println("sequence ${sequence.frameCount} frames; capacity $capacity splats")
              println("  (the true peak over any $slots consecutive frames, not the $slots largest anywhere)")

              /*
              Each capture is a depth map from a camera at the origin looking down +z, so its content
              already sits ~1-1.6 in front of its own origin. A ring around the viewer is therefore
              fifteen rotations about Y and no translation: every panel lands at its natural distance.
              */
              fun yRotation(radians: Double): Matrix4f {
                  val c = Math.cos(radians).toFloat()
                  val s = Math.sin(radians).toFloat()
                  // Matrix4f is column-major, m<column><row>: each group of four is a COLUMN.
                  return Matrix4f()
                      .set(
                          c,
                          0f,
                          -s,
                          0f,
                          0f,
                          1f,
                          0f,
                          0f,
                          s,
                          0f,
                          c,
                          0f,
                          0f,
                          0f,
                          0f,
                          1f,
                      )
              }
              val arc = Math.toRadians(arcDegrees)
              val ring =
                  (0 until slots).map { i ->
                      yRotation(-arc / 2.0 + arc * i / (slots - 1).coerceAtLeast(1))
                  }

              val cloud = GaussianSplatRenderer.streaming(
                  capacity = capacity,
                  renderer = renderer,
                  config = GaussianSplatRenderer.Config(
                      sortMode = SortMode.None, // packInto writes back-to-front instead
                      blend = blend,
                      sizeScale = splatSize,
                      colorGamma = colorGamma,
                  ),
                  name = "splatStream",
              )
              // Depth-map convention: +z forward, +y DOWN, hence up = (0, -1, 0).
              cloud.camera.at = Vector3f(0f, -cameraUp, -cameraBack)
              cloud.camera.target = Vector3f(0f, 0f, 1.2f)
              cloud.camera.up = Vector3f(0f, -1f, 0f)
              cloud.alphaScale = alphaBoost
              cloud.install()

              val scratch = GaussianSplatRenderer.PackScratch()

              /*
              ---- the play head. Select a line and run it as a fragment while this plays ----------
              transport.playing = false          pause
              transport.normalized = 0.42        scrub to 42% of the shot
              transport.seek(60.0)               scrub to frame 60
              transport.scrubBy(-1.0)            step back one frame
              transport.speed = -0.25            slow reverse
              transport.loop = false             clamp at the ends instead of wrapping
              */
              val transport = SplatTransport(sequence.frameCount, fps = fps)
              // -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

              var packedMs = 0.0
              var decodes = 0
              var displayFrames = 0

              renderer.renderList.preTargets["__splat_feed__"] = Target { _, _ ->
                  displayFrames++
                  /*
                  False on the display frames where the resolved frame did not move -- six in seven at
                  12 fps into 90 Hz -- and false for a scrub that stays inside one frame. Each false is
                  fifteen files not re-decoded to write identical bytes.
                  */
                  if (!transport.advance(System.nanoTime())) return@Target
                  val at = transport.frame
                  val sources =
                      (0 until slots).map { slot ->
                          SplatSource(sequence.raw(at + slot), ring[slot])
                      }
                  val t0 = System.nanoTime()
                  cloud.reupload(
                      sources,
                      sortAlong = if (sortEachFrame) Vector3f(0f, 0f, 1f) else null,
                      scratch = scratch,
                  )
                  packedMs = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1e6
                  decodes++
              }

              var reportedAt = System.nanoTime()
              renderer.renderList.preTargets["__splat_report__"] = Target { _, _ ->
                  val now = System.nanoTime()
                  if (now - reportedAt < 1_000_000_000L) return@Target
                  reportedAt = now
                  println(
                      "frame ${transport.frame}/${sequence.frameCount}  " +
                          "$decodes decode(s) in $displayFrames display frame(s)  " +
                          "last pack %.1f ms  %s".format(packedMs, sequence.stats),
                  )
                  decodes = 0
                  displayFrames = 0
              }

              println("streaming ${sequence.frameCount} frames at $fps fps, sort=$sortEachFrame")
              println(
                  "blend=${if (blend.orderIndependent) "order-independent, the sort is optional" else "Over, needs the back-to-front order"}",
              )
          }
  - connect:
      parent: agent_graphics_context
      child: splat_sequence_streaming
  - execute:
      box: splat_sequence_streaming
      property: code
